story: On Magnolia Loop, Gary squints at the bulletin board in the humid afternoon haze, hoping to find his Architectural Review decision on his golf cart application. Over at the Rec Center, Donna is warming up with dinking drills on pickleball court one while she waits for him to report back. Hal is out on the street counting the flamingos in the Donna flock, dutifully keeping track of every pink bird. Meanwhile, Rosa stands at the Architectural Review desk in Town Hall, determinedly handing in the parade cart folder with Gary's clamp list, light layout, and a plain description of the tuck-on decorations.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Check for a posted Architectural Review decision on my cart application
Donna (pickleball court 1): Warm up with some dinking drills while waiting for Gary
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street
Rosa (architectural review desk): Hand in the parade cart folder with Gary's clamp list, light layout, and a plain description of the tuck-on decorations

gary.thought_process: Hal's busy counting Donna's flamingos, and he already heard my whole plan last tick: cart stays in the garage until Architectural Review signs off, Rosa's got the sketches at the desk. No sense repeating myself. The bulletin board is right here and I keep hoping the approval notice is posted, so I'll check it. If nothing's up, I'll head home and keep bench-testing the wiring in the garage, which is the legal way to keep the parade plan moving.

parameters.content: Check for a posted Architectural Review decision on my cart application

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with no one around, and I already studied the ladder standings and reserved a two-hour court last tick, which fits the L-05 limit. I've got what I came for. Gary has never played, so I should get him out here and start drilling third-shot drops before the ladder match. The courts are empty, so it's a good moment to warm up and size up our competition, then catch Gary when he shows. I'll practice dinking on court 1 and keep the momentum going.

parameters.content: Warm up with some dinking drills while waiting for Gary

hal.thought_process: Gary has said twice now that the cart stays in the garage until Architectural Review signs off, so there's nothing left to chase on that front. I came out here with a second item on my list: Donna's flamingos. I told her straight before, and the street's own count is the proof the committee will want. Code L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street, so I'll tally what's actually out here instead of going on memory. By the book, and fair to the neighbor.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street

rosa.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall with the parade cart folder, and I already said I was submitting it at the architectural review desk last tick. Gary's clamp list and light layout are in there, and I want to be upfront with Review about everything we're adding, since Donna's tuck-on plan is only clever if we're honest about it. No one else is around, so I'll just do it myself. Once it's filed, I can get back to prepping for Thursday and the community I'm trying to build.

parameters.content: Hand in the parade cart folder with Gary's clamp list, light layout, and a plain description of the tuck-on decorations

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
